newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks off slightly by lunch on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks off slightly by lunch on profit taking.

text.p: The Thai bourse, in the positive zone all morning, fell just before the lunch break on Tuesday on sales of some large capitalised stocks ahead of an announcement on IMF-supported economic measures, brokers said.

"The market declined on profit-taking as investors thought the market had risen quite high at the open this morning. Investors are still waiting for details of the IMF economic rescue package for Thailand," said Busaba Kunasirin of Chao Phya Finance.
The composite SET index retreated 0.10 point to 663.72 on 2.1 billion baht turnover by the lunch break.
Brokers said investors were waiting to hear details of the IMF rescue measures aimed at healing Thailand's ailing economy.
Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya is scheduled to hold a news conference later on Tuesday after the cabinet discusses the proposed IMF plans.

Nava Finance topped the active list, gaining 0.50 baht to 33.00. In the banking sector, Thai Farmers, which opened at 119, fell one to 116, while Bangkok Bank declined three to 171. -- Suthep Chawla (662) 652-0642, email: bangkok.newsroom@reuters.com
